From: Buddy Williams <buddy.williams@insurity.com>
Subject: State-sync: disjoint per-node nodes.json fork becomes an unrecoverable hard conflict when the merge baseline is missing (needs manual state-recovery)

Body:
Subject: State-sync: disjoint per-node nodes.json fork becomes an unrecoverable hard conflict when the merge baseline is missing (needs manual state-recovery)

Severity: High �X halts all-node state synchronization; dashboard shows "counts are non-authoritative"; requires manual
operator recovery.

Environment
- Target app: /insurity/ProSuite, node bo2lnxnevo03-buddy, runtime root /insurity/refine/run/8082.
- Build: bin/refine deployed 2026-08-17 09:27 (the release that added the state_sync_stale_threshold_seconds default
and dropped worktree_cleanup_generated_paths).
- Fleet: 5 registered nodes; at time of incident only this node was live.

Symptom
Dashboard banner: "State sync has failed since 2026-08-17T11:58:56Z. All-node counts are local and non-authoritative
until synchronization recovers." Health record: status: failed, last_error: "Refine state changed on multiple nodes
during first_pass: 1 unresolved path(s)", unresolved_paths: ["nodes.json"].

What triggered it
The 09:27 release performs a settings-schema migration. On first load+save after deploy, each node normalized its own
nodes.json entry (added state_sync_stale_threshold_seconds, removed worktree_cleanup_generated_paths). This node's
entry migrated at 11:29; the QA node (default) migrated at 11:28. Each side changed only its own record from a shared
pre-migration base �X i.e. a disjoint, per-node divergence.

Expected
merge_node_registry (src/tools/host/git_sync/node_registry_merge.rs:18) is explicitly built for this: last-writer-wins
per node id, retaining one-sided changes. The disjoint case is covered by the
disjoint_heartbeat_updates_merge_by_node_id unit test. It should have auto-resolved with no operator involvement.

Actual �X root cause
In prepare_semantic_state_changes (src/tools/host/git_sync/service.rs:426�V455), the merge only runs if the
common-ancestor bytes can be loaded:

let Some(base_bytes) = self.load_baseline_file(state_root, &relative, *base_fingerprint)? else {
  continue;   // baseline unrecoverable -> path left unresolved -> hard conflict
};
...
let Some(merged) = merged else { continue; };

load_baseline_file (state_worktree.rs:296�V315) recovers the base content by scanning refine/state history for a
revision whose content matches the stored fingerprint. If that fingerprint's bytes are not reachable in history �X or
the baseline fingerprint file (.git/refine-state-baseline.json) is stale/absent �X it returns None, the merge is
silently skipped via continue, and nodes.json is reported as an unresolved first_pass conflict.

Net effect: a fork the semantic merge is designed to resolve becomes a hard, sync-blocking conflict, solely because
the base couldn't be reconstructed. On this host the baseline file was dated 10:12 (stale relative to the 11:28/11:29
migration), consistent with this path. We suspect the baseline went stale/missing around the earlier runtime-root
migration (two runtime roots have bitten us before).

Contributing issue #1 �X silent skip, no diagnostic
When load_baseline_file returns None, there's no log/telemetry distinguishing "genuine multi-writer conflict" from
"couldn't reconstruct base, so I gave up." Operators can't tell a real conflict from a recoverable-but-skipped one.

Contributing issue #2 �X recovery preview is unusable while automation runs
Each failed sync attempt appends a state_sync activity entry into live .refine state (see append_state_sync_activity),
which mutates the live snapshot. state-recovery preview fences on a stable live snapshot and aborts with "the live
state snapshot changed" (recovery/service.rs:141,200). Because the failing sync loop writes on every attempt, preview
fails every time until automation is paused. We observed 3/3 preview failures back-to-back; it only succeeded after
refine workflow pause. The recovery tool the error message tells you to run doesn't work in the state it's advertised
for.

Contributing issue #3 �X no backoff on a persistent conflict (amplifies #2)
On a non-transient conflict the sync worker keeps retrying at the debounce cadence (state_sync_debounce_seconds,
default 5s; schedule.rs) with no failure backoff. attempt_sequence advanced ~1000 (22512 �� 23542) in minutes, each
attempt re-appending activity-log churn. This both spams the activity log and sustains the snapshot churn in #2.
(Related to the still-pending backoff/GC work noted from the earlier claims-bloat incident.)

Impact on multi-node recovery (why this matters now)
Three nodes are currently shut down and will restart on the new binary. On startup each will re-migrate its own
nodes.json entry (self-update) while its local refine/state is behind origin �X the same disjoint per-node divergence.
They should auto-merge on their first project sync only if their baseline is intact and the base bytes are reachable
in refine/state history. Any node whose baseline went stale (same runtime-root history as this one) will reproduce
this hard conflict on startup and need manual state-recovery. A raw git pull is not a safe substitute �X it invokes
git's line-level merge on nodes.json instead of the semantic per-node merge and can leave the worktree conflicted.

Workaround that resolved it (for reference)
1. refine workflow pause (stops the failing-sync churn so preview can get a stable snapshot).
2. refine project state-recovery preview �� apply --authority remote (QA treated as authoritative for the registry).
3. refine project sync (settles health, refreshes baseline, re-normalizes this node's entry, pushes to origin).
4. refine workflow resume.
Post-fix: last_attempt_outcome: succeeded, all failure/stale/error fields cleared; both migrated node entries
identical on live and remote.

Suggested fixes for dev to consider
1. When load_baseline_file returns None for a disjoint per-node change, fall back to a base-less 2-way per-node
reconcile (LWW by updated_at) instead of continue, or at minimum emit a distinct, logged outcome ("merge skipped: base
unrecoverable") rather than a generic hard conflict.
2. Make state-recovery preview/apply resilient to the sync worker's own activity-log writes �X e.g. exclude state_sync
activity appends from the stale-fence snapshot, or auto-quiesce sync for the duration of a preview, so recovery works
without a manual pause.
3. Add failure backoff to the sync scheduler so a persistent conflict doesn't retry every ~5s indefinitely and
self-amplify via activity-log churn.
4. Investigate why the baseline (.git/refine-state-baseline.json) went stale/unrecoverable �X likely tied to the
runtime-root migration; ensure save_state_baseline runs (and history retains the fingerprinted bytes) across
runtime-root moves.

Artifacts available on request: conflict report run/8082/state-sync-conflicts/latest.json, health record
run/8082/state-sync-health.json, recovery manifest under ProSuite/.git/refine-state-recoveries/.

findings.description: P3 does not define a crash-consistent versioned association between the fingerprint map and its retained Git snapshot, so a process stop between updating the ref and replacing the baseline file can pair fingerprints with the wrong commit or orphan the intended evidence.
findings.recommendation: Store and validate the exact snapshot OID or immutable ref in backward-compatible baseline metadata, publish the anchor before atomically replacing that metadata, and retire the previous anchor only after the new pair is durable.

findings.description: P5 assumes state-sync activity is inside the recovery stale fence, but current durable-state enumeration already excludes the entire logs namespace containing logs/activity.jsonl, so the plan has not identified the actual included path or writer that caused the observed three preview failures.
findings.recommendation: Add a reproducing test or path-level diagnostic that proves which fenced input changes, then serialize or exclude only that verified node-local input while preserving all durable live-state, head, identity, and decision fences.

findings.description: No checklist item requires regression verification for the new fallback, retained-anchor restart behavior, recovery concurrency, diagnostics, or scheduler backoff and manual bypass, leaving the high-risk fail-closed and crash-safety contracts unprotected.
findings.recommendation: Add focused first-pass and push-retry merge tests, malformed and equal-time rejection tests, interruption and legacy-baseline tests, concurrent preview tests, and deterministic backoff reset, suppression, cap, and explicit-sync bypass tests.

result.summary: Close three safety gaps before implementing the otherwise well-scoped state-sync recovery plan.

checklist.description: Refactor semantic reconciliation to distinguish a wholly absent synchronization baseline from unavailable bytes for a recorded path and carry structured baseline-reconstruction outcomes through both first-pass and push-retry handling.

Add a nodes.json-only two-way fallback for unavailable recorded baseline bytes that validates both registries, retains the canonical node-id union, selects unequal versions only by comparable updated_at values, and leaves malformed data or equal-time disagreement unresolved without extending fallback authority to Goals or a wholly absent baseline.

Version the backward-compatible baseline metadata with the exact immutable snapshot OID or ref that owns its fingerprint map, publish and durably validate the new anchor before atomically replacing the metadata, and retire the previous anchor only after the new pair is durable so interruption cannot misassociate or orphan evidence.

Resolve recorded path bytes from the metadata-bound retained snapshot before the legacy history scan and report distinct structured outcomes when reconstruction fails, the safe node-registry fallback succeeds, or semantic reconciliation remains unresolved in sync details, health errors, and complete conflict reports.

Add path-level stale-fence diagnostics and a reproducing concurrent-sync recovery case to identify the actual fenced input and writer, then serialize that verified writer with preview and apply snapshot capture or exclude only a proven node-local nonsynchronizable input while preserving every durable live-state, remote-state, head, identity, and decision fence.

Introduce capped in-memory exponential backoff for repeated unchanged background sync failures, reset it on success or meaningful target, node, local-state, or failure-context change, and keep explicit project sync immediately available without emitting attempts or activity during suppressed intervals.

Add focused regression coverage for first-pass and push-retry fallback success, malformed and equal-time rejection, retained-anchor interruption and legacy metadata loading, recovery concurrency and changed-path diagnostics, and deterministic backoff suppression, reset, cap, and explicit-sync bypass behavior.

Update only the affected target-app, fleet, and activity-evidence intent pages to document the narrow base-less node-registry rule, versioned retained baseline anchor, recovery snapshot boundary, diagnostic outcomes, and background-failure backoff.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: P3 now makes the baseline fingerprint map and retained snapshot a versioned, validated pair, orders anchor publication before atomic metadata replacement, and keeps the previous anchor until the new pair is durable.

P5 no longer assumes activity logs are fenced; it requires changed-path evidence and a reproducing concurrent-sync case before coordinating the verified writer or narrowly excluding a proven node-local input while retaining all authoritative fences.

P7 adds focused regression coverage for both merge paths, rejection cases, interruption and legacy anchor behavior, recovery concurrency and diagnostics, and every scheduler backoff and manual-bypass contract.

result.summary: Make node-registry synchronization converge safely when recorded baseline bytes are unavailable by adding a narrowly fail-closed two-way fallback, crash-consistent retained evidence, actionable diagnostics, stable recovery coordination, and bounded retry backoff.

governance_precheck.message: The finalized plan does not require any governance or constitutional violation.

checklist.evidence: Separated absent baseline metadata from unavailable recorded bytes and introduced structured per-path reconstruction and reconciliation outcomes used in first-pass and push-retry handling.

Added a nodes.json-only two-way fallback that validates both NodeRegistry values, retains the canonical id union, requires strictly comparable updated_at ordering for unequal shared records, and rejects malformed or equal-time disagreement; missing whole-baseline and Goal paths remain fail closed.

Baseline metadata v2 binds fingerprints to an exact snapshot OID and unique refs/refine/state-baseline anchor; the anchor and owned state map are synced and validated before atomic metadata replacement, and stale anchors are retired only afterward while legacy maps remain readable.

Recorded bytes resolve from the metadata-bound retained snapshot before legacy history; sync details distinguish safe fallback success, health errors name unavailable bytes or semantic rejection, and versioned complete conflict reports persist structured outcomes.

Recovery previews now capture under the repository operation lock already held by apply and sync, previews carry per-path fingerprints, and stale errors name changed durable paths. Regression evidence confirms concurrent sync-owned writes wait for preview; it also proves node-local state_sync activity logs were already excluded from the durable snapshot and require no new fence exception.

Added capped in-memory exponential background-failure backoff keyed by target, node, local fingerprint, and failure context; success and meaningful scope changes reset it, suppressed intervals launch no health attempt or activity, and explicit project sync remains outside and bypasses background suppression.

Added focused tests for first-pass and push-retry fallback, malformed/equal-time rejection, retained-anchor interruption and legacy load, recovery concurrency and exact changed paths, activity exclusion, and deterministic backoff growth, reset, cap, suppression, and explicit bypass.
Updated only target-app, fleet, and activity-evidence intent pages for the fallback authority, retained snapshot pair, recovery boundary and diagnostics, structured outcomes, and background backoff.
